Healthy Pumpkin Pie Bars

Jump to Recipe
by Lily Ernst on September 26, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:14
Instaread

These Healthy Pumpkin Pie Bars have all the cozy flavors of classic pumpkin pie in an easy-to-make bar form. Made with oat flour, almond flour, and Greek yogurt, and naturally sweetened with maple syrup, they’re creamy, satisfying, and perfect for fall gatherings, holiday dessert tables, or a wholesome afternoon treat.



 
  • Why you’ll love this recipe:
  • Ingredients you’ll need:
  • How to make healthy pumpkin pie bars:
  • 🌟 Expert tips:
  • Storing & freezing instructions:
  • Recipe FAQs:
  • Healthy Pumpkin Pie Bars

Why you’ll love this recipe:

  • Healthier than traditional pumpkin pie – Made with wholesome ingredients like oat flour, almond flour, Greek yogurt, and natural sweeteners for a lighter dessert.
  • Easy to make ahead – These bars need time to chill, making them perfect for holiday entertaining and meal prep.
  • Creamy, rich pumpkin flavor – The smooth pumpkin filling tastes just like classic pumpkin pie, with warm fall spices in every bite.

If you are looking for more healthy pumpkin recipes, try my Healthy Pumpkin Pie, Healthy Pumpkin Bread, and Healthy Pumpkin Bars.

Ingredients you’ll need:

  • Oat flour – Provides structure and a tender texture while adding fiber and whole-grain goodness to the crust.
  • Almond flour – Creates a rich, buttery crust and helps keep the bars naturally gluten-free.
  • Maple syrup (crust) – Sweetens the crust naturally while helping bind the ingredients together.
  • Salted butter – Adds moisture, richness, and flavor while helping the crust hold its shape. Also naturally sweetens the filling.
  • Pumpkin puree – Forms the base of the filling, providing moisture, creaminess, and classic pumpkin flavor.
  • Greek yogurt – Adds protein and a creamy texture while making the filling lighter than traditional pumpkin pie.
  • Coconut sugar – Adds a subtle, caramel-like sweetness and depth of flavor.
  • Eggs – Help bind the filling and give the bars their smooth, sliceable custardy texture.
  • Pumpkin pie spice – Provides the warm blend of cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves that gives pumpkin desserts their signature fall flavor.
  • Salt – Enhances the sweetness and balances the flavors throughout the filling.

How to make healthy pumpkin pie bars:

(The full written and printable recipe is further below.)

Step #1) In a medium bowl, toss together the oat flour and almond flour. Stir in the maple syrup and butter until all is moist.

Step #2) Evenly press the mixture into a parchment paper-lined 9×13″ pan. Bake at 350F for 10 minutes.

Step #3) Meanwhile, whisk together the pumpkin puree, Greek yogurt, maple syrup, coconut sugar, eggs, pumpkin pie spice, and salt in a large bowl.

Step #4) Pour the mixture over the hot crust and place it back in the oven for 50-55 minutes or until the center is almost set.

🌟 Expert tips:

  • Use pure pumpkin puree, not pumpkin pie filling.
  • For the cleanest slices, chill the bars overnight before cutting.
  • Line the pan with parchment paper for easy removal and neat edges.
  • Wipe your knife clean between cuts for bakery-style squares.

Storing & freezing instructions:

Storing – Store pumpkin pie bars in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. The flavor actually improves after a day, as the spices have time to develop.

Freezing – Place chilled bars in a freezer-safe container with parchment paper between layers and freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before serving.

Recipe FAQs:

Can I use honey instead of maple syrup?

Yes, honey can be substituted for the maple syrup, although the flavor will be slightly different.

Why do my pumpkin pie bars need to chill?

Chilling allows the filling to fully set, making the bars easier to slice and giving them the classic pumpkin pie texture.

Can I use homemade pumpkin puree?

Absolutely. Just make sure it’s thick and well-drained so the filling isn’t too watery.

Can I make these ahead of time?

Yes! They’re an excellent make-ahead dessert and can be prepared up to two days in advance.

Healthy Pumpkin Pie Bars

Yield: 18
Prep: 20 minutes mins
Cook: 1 hour hr
Chill Time: 4 hours hrs
Total: 5 hours hrs 20 minutes mins
Author: Lily Ernst
Course: Dessert
Method: Bake
These Healthy Pumpkin Pie Bars have all the cozy flavors of classic pumpkin pie in an easy-to-make bar form. Made with oat flour, almond flour, and Greek yogurt, and naturally sweetened with maple syrup.
Print Leave a Review Pin Recipe

Ingredients

  • 2 cup almond flour
  • 1 cups oat flour
  • 1/3 cup maple syrup
  • 1/4 cup salted butter
  • 3 cups pumpkin puree
  • 1 cup Greek yogurt
  • 1/2 cup maple syrup
  • 1/4 cup coconut sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 2 tsp pumpkin pie spice
  • 1/2 tsp salt
Prevent your screen from going dark

Instructions
 

  • Preheat oven to 350F. Line and grease a 9×13" pan with parchment paper.
  • In a medium bowl, toss the almond flour and oat flour together. Stir in the maple syrup and butter until all is moist.
    2 cup almond flour, 1 cups oat flour, 1/3 cup maple syrup, 1/4 cup salted butter
  • Press the mixture evenly into the prepared pan. Bake for 10 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden.
  • Meanwhile, whisk together the pumpkin puree, Greek yogurt, maple syrup, coconut sugar, eggs, pumpkin pie spice, and salt in a large bowl.
    3 cups pumpkin puree, 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1/2 cup maple syrup, 1/4 cup coconut sugar, 2 large eggs, 2 tsp pumpkin pie spice, 1/2 tsp salt
  • Pour the mixture over the hot crust and place it back in the oven for 50-55 minutes or until the center is almost set.
  • Let cool to room temperature. Then cover and chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours, or overnight, to set before slicing and serving.

Notes

Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
